chunks: They were only confused dreams," they said; "we do not know how to interpret them."
ai.seo_question: What did the Egyptians mean by calling Joseph's dream 'adghathu ahlan'?
ai.summary: In this verse, the Egyptian courtiers describe Joseph's (AS) dream as 'adghathu ahlan' (confused or mixed-up dreams), admitting their own lack of expertise in interpretation to emphasize the divine origin of his gift. This moment serves as a crucial narrative pivot, contrasting human limitation with the prophetic insight that will soon elevate Joseph to a position of authority in Egypt. The admission of ignorance underscores the theme of divine selection, a key motif in Shia exegesis regarding the infallible knowledge granted to the Imams.
